name: AI GridWatch data center project tracker
caveat:
A working set of identified proposals a community can track, not a census — most of the country's activity is not in here yet. Pennsylvania is the exception: its rows are synced from PA DEP's own data-center permit tracker, so the state's coverage is close to complete and carries the permit trail with it.

**Each row carries its own provenance.** Rows showing a verification date link to reporting or the governing body's own record and were read on that date; rows marked *unverified* have no source on record — a lead to check, not a fact to cite.

**Stage is derived, not asserted.** *Hearing scheduled*, *Awaiting decision*, *Approved* and *Withdrawn* are computed from each row's milestone dates on every rebuild, so a hearing date that has passed stops reading 'scheduled'. Hearings get moved and projects re-file under new names — treat a scheduled date as the earliest to act by, and confirm with the clerk before relying on it. Leads are mined into data/project_candidates.json and promoted here only after a human reads a primary source.

schema.name: Project or code name.
schema.filing_llc: Shell LLC on the filing (ties to the campus registry), or blank.
schema.locality: Town or county the project sits in.
schema.size_mw: Planned IT/critical load in MW, or blank.
schema.announced: ISO date first publicly proposed, or blank.
schema.rezoning_filed: ISO date the rezoning/permit application was filed, or blank.
schema.hearing_date: ISO date of the next/decisive public hearing, or blank.
schema.decided_date: ISO date a terminal decision was reached, or blank.
schema.outcome: approved | denied | withdrawn | blank (blank = still live).
schema.stage: DERIVED status shown on the page (Hearing scheduled, Awaiting decision, In review, Proposed, Rumored, Approved, Under construction, Operating, Denied, Withdrawn, Blocked by ban).
schema.days_to_hearing: DERIVED days until the hearing (negative once past), or blank.
schema.source: Primary URL backing the current status.
schema.as_of: ISO date the source was read, or blank.
schema.verified: true if a source is on record.

projects.name: Google West Memphis
projects.note: $4B, 1,178-acre campus with 5 buildings in West Memphis, Arkansas. Under construction.

events.summary: Groot LLC, a Google-linked entity, paid $16.5 million to buy roughly 1,117 acres of agricultural land on Bollinger Road in West Memphis, Crittenden County.

West Memphis City Council unanimously approved a MOU, development agreement, and PILOT incentive package with Groot LLC for a project valued at up to $10 billion, with potential for up to $50 billion in personal-property tax abatements over 30 years.
Entergy Arkansas and Google jointly sought Arkansas Public Service Commission approval of a special electricity rate contract to power the West Memphis data center.
Reporting confirmed Google (via Groot LLC) as the company behind the planned $10 billion, five-building data center campus on 1,178 acres south of Bollinger Road, dubbed Project Pyramid.

Google, the Governor, and state/local officials formally announced a $4 billion AI/cloud data center project in West Memphis — Google first data center in Arkansas — with a $25 million Energy Impact Fund for low-income households in Crittenden County.

Entergy Arkansas announced it would power the Google project with a 600 MW Cypress Solar project and 350 MW of battery storage, with Google saying the deal would deliver over $1.1 billion in net benefits to Entergy customers.

Arkansas PSC held a hearing on the special rate contract between Entergy and Google; the public was asked to leave during portions covering confidential contract details, drawing transparency criticism.

Arkansas PSC approved Entergy special rate contract with Google but denied the utility requested ratemaking treatment and deferred a decision on investment tax credit treatment for the Cypress Solar facility.
Arkansas Advocate reported state officials were largely declining to scrutinize fiscal and environmental tradeoffs of the data center boom out of fear of losing investment to other states.
Arkansas PSC issued a follow-up order reversing itself to allow investment tax credits from the Cypress Solar facility to be used in pricing under the Google contract.
Google began actively hiring for electrical engineer and facilities technician roles at the West Memphis data center, which remained under construction with an expected 18-24 month build timeline.
Reporting revealed Google and Entergy were keeping the full terms of their energy rate contract sealed/confidential, raising transparency concerns among ratepayer advocates.
Reporting detailed that bond issuances tied to the West Memphis Google data center PILOT financing could total as much as $60 billion in permanent financing authority over the deal 30-year term.
At an Arkansas PSC hearing on Entergy proposed residential rate increase, speakers including the Little Rock NAACP chapter head cited the sealed Google contract as evidence of a lack of transparency.
